notes: Checked: the 18 key claims, plus ACDC's tracr result, Lettvin's electrode-paper anecdote and Tracr's section numbers. Confirmed against primary text: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 18 (18 is now confirmed from the primary EDVAC transcription). Claim 4 also gets a note that Kleene's 1951 star is binary (E*F). Claim 14 is accurate but incomplete; more Percepta citation sites were added.

corrections.original: Siegelmann and Sontag proved that a fixed finite recurrent net ... can simulate any Turing machine in real time.
corrections.fix: 1992 (COLT): 'one can do this in linear time'. 1995 (JCSS): 'one can simulate any multi-stack Turing machine in real time'. State it as linear time for Turing machines in general, real time for multi-stack machines.

Issue date is 3 Jan 2020 (Science 367(6473):83-87, PMID 31896716); it was released online 2 Jan. Abstract wording verified: 'In contrast to typical all-or-none action potentials, dCaAPs were graded' ... 'classify linearly nonseparable inputs-a computation conventionally thought to require multilayered networks.'

corrections.original: Giannou et al. ... a looped 13-layer transformer ... acts as a small instruction-set computer (abstract quote incl. 'even shallow transformers can execute full-fledged, general-purpose programs').
corrections.fix: '13-layer' and the 'shallow transformers' sentence are in the arXiv abstract only. The ICML/PMLR abstract says 'constant depth looped transformer network'. In the paper, the FLEQ machine has '9 + max{l1,...,lM}' layers (Theorem 1); the 13-layer figures are Lemmas 6-8 (1 head). SUBLEQ Lemma 4 (ten layers, two heads) is confirmed.

corrections.original: ACDC 'achieved poor performance on both tracr tasks' in one figure, a reminder that compiled models differ from trained ones.
corrections.fix: The inference is unsupported. The same sentence continues: 'but the circuit was perfectly recovered by ACDC at any threshold τ >0 when patching activations with zeros'. The poor result reflects the patching distribution and metric.

corrections.original: Tracr quotes ('we will likely never compile fully featured language models'; microscope lens) located at §7
corrections.fix: Wording verified verbatim in v5. The section number '§7' was not confirmed, so the location now reads 'closing discussion, Limitations paragraph (v5)'.

corrections.original: Arbitrarily small analog noise reduces such nets to finite automata (Maass & Orponen 1998).
corrections.fix: The Maass & Orponen result is confirmed verbatim. The robustness question is contested: Siegelmann & Sontag 1994 claimed their models 'exhibit at least some robustness with respect to noise and implementation errors'. The dossier notes both sides.

corrections.original: The frog's-eye paper ... concluded that 'the eye speaks to the brain in a language already highly organized and interpreted', undercutting the pure logic-gate picture.
corrections.fix: The quote is verified verbatim (Proc. IRE 47(11), p. 1950). 'Undercutting the logic-gate picture' is later interpretation by Gefter and Lettvin ('It disappointed him'); the 1959 paper makes no such claim. Narrate it as interpretation.

corrections.original: The prevailing engineering belief favors learned weights: Sutton's 'The Bitter Lesson' (2019)...
corrections.fix: Sutton's date (13 Mar 2019) and quotes are verified. It is a dominant position, not a consensus: Rodney Brooks, 'A Better Lesson' (19 Mar 2019): 'I think Sutton is wrong for a number of reasons.' The claim is now marked contested, with the dissent sourced.

corrections.original: Lettvin traded the IRE an electrode paper for publishing this one (as reported in secondary sources).
corrections.fix: No source was cited or found. Demoted to UNVERIFIED; do not narrate.
